summary: Old Yaquina Bay Lighthouse at Newport, Oregon: lit in 1871, put out in 1874, a museum since the 1960s, and a modern privately maintained light since 1996.

lens.note: Fifth-order Fresnel lens in the 1871 light, with a whale oil lamp most likely (NRHP)

structures.material: frame (redwood siding) on a brick basement
structures.note: Two-story house with a square lantern platform on the east side

staffing.note: One keeper, Charles H. Peirce, 1871-1874 (NRHP; USLHS)

access.note: Owned by Oregon State Parks, managed by Friends of Yaquina Lighthouses; open daily noon to 4 p.m., per LighthouseFriends (check hours)

facts.agency: Oregon State Parks (owner); Friends of Yaquina Lighthouses (manager); modern light privately maintained under Coast Guard certification (LighthouseFriends)

events.note: Constructed May to October 1871; two principal contracts (Bien, lantern and ironwork, 16 June 1871; Simpson, labor, 19 June 1871)
Sale considered; offer too small, property retained (LighthouseFriends)
Roof and outside sheathing renewed to keep the building from going to ruin
Army Corps of Engineers granted permission to occupy the house during the Yaquina jetty work (NRHP; LighthouseFriends: 1888 to 1896)
Lightning struck the house in a thunderstorm on 17 November 1889 (Morning Oregonian, dateline Newport, 17 Nov.); badly splintered
Life-Saving Service crew quarters and lookout; use ended 1933
Released by the federal government to the State of Oregon for highway and park purposes
Dedicated as a historical site under the Lincoln County Historical Society
Operated as a museum by the County Historical Society from 1965 (NRHP)
National Register nomination signed March 1974; Oregon State Parks begins year-long restoration
Year-long restoration by Oregon State Parks
Relit 7 December 1996 with a 250mm modern optic donated by James Gibbs; USCG privately maintained aid; fixed white, six miles
$1.6 million exterior restoration; lantern room refurbished in Alabama and lifted back on 12 August 2025; reopened to visitors that fall

corrections.why: The historic light was first lit in November 1871 (LighthouseFriends: 3 November; NRHP: November 1871). The 1996 date is the relighting of the site with a modern optic.
NRHP: constructed May to October 1871. 1870 is the year Congress made the appropriation (LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NRHP says the Yaquina Head light lies three miles north of the bay light. LighthouseFriends says four miles. The story reports both.
NRHP: a wife and eight children. LighthouseFriends: six children on arrival, and a ninth child born in March 1872. The count is not settled, and the story says so.
USLHS roster: Peirce. NRHP: Pierce. LighthouseFriends: Peirce, pronounced Purse. The story uses Peirce and notes the variant.
NRHP: Sophronia S. Baldwin. LighthouseFriends: Sophrina. The story uses the NRHP spelling.
NRHP: James S. Polhemus, chief local engineer. LighthouseFriends: John Polhemus. The 1889 Oregonian: J.S. Polhemus. The story says 'Polhemus' and quotes the newspaper's J.S.
NRHP says Royal A. Bensell publicized the entrance to the Yaquina as a harbor of refuge; it does not say the bay served as one by itself. The story attributes the promotion to Bensell.

notes_for_editor: Revised 2026-10-27 by the independent fact-check. Corrections made: 'the early 1870s' is now 1869 (LighthouseFriends dates the most-populated-port description to the February 1869 memorial period); the NRHP's 'harbor of refuge' is attributed to Royal A. Bensell's promotion of the entrance, not to the bay as a harbor of refuge; 'both contracts are in the National Archives' is replaced with the NRHP's wording (construction records in the National Archives show two principal contracts); 'the government considered selling' is now 'an effort was made to sell' (LighthouseFriends); the lightning date is 17 November 1889 (the Oregonian dateline), not 'November'; the first sentence now has a footnote; footnote 4 gives the LighthouseFriends URL. Copyright: LighthouseFriends text is paraphrased, with the only quotes being from the public-domain NRHP and the 1889 newspaper as LighthouseFriends quotes it. The USLHS place record lists 'Private Aid: Yes', 'Active Aid to Navigation: Yes' and a position (44 62.41 N, 124 06.29 W) that is not a valid minute reading; the story does not use the place position. The USLHS place page prints the height of light above mean high water as 161 ft (about 49 m); the earlier draft's 50.3 m figure is not in the place page and is not used in the story. Caretaker Royal A. Bensell is reported by the NRHP only and is not put on the roster. The 1870-1874 Light-House Board reports are not in the corpus (its lhb series starts in 1891). The 1974 NRHP form is dated March 1974; the NRHP listing date itself was not checked beyond LighthouseFriends' statement that the listing came in 1974. Living people: James Gibbs is named as the published donor of the 1996 optic (LighthouseFriends), in his public role only. The 1889 Polhemus family and the Bensells are historical figures. LighthouseFriends' visitor hours and the 2025 restoration status were not checked against Oregon State Parks; the story says hours may have changed.
